chunks: Ahmad ibn 'Abdun narrated to us from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Zubayr, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jamilah, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who fasted, then presumed that night had entered and the sun had set, and there was cloud cover in the sky, so he broke his fast, then the clouds cleared and behold, the sun had not yet set. He said: His fast is complete and he does not need to make it up.

key_terms.وَلَا يَقْضِيهِ: and he does not make it up

ai.seo_question: Does a person need to make up their fast if they break it due to clouds but the sun is still visible?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the principle of *al-istishab* (presumption of continuity) in fasting, where a reasonable doubt regarding sunset due to cloud cover validates the fast even if the sun remains visible. It highlights the Shia juristic preference for ease (*rukhas*) when a person acts on a plausible presumption (*zann*) rather than certainty, ensuring the fast is not invalidated by subsequent clarification. This ruling underscores the importance of subjective certainty in ritual acts, distinguishing it from cases where one is certain they broke the fast before actual sunset.
